title: CacheBlend Quality-Only Reproduction on Mistral-7B (HF transformers, from scratch)

strategy.justification: The official YaoJiayi/CacheBlend repo is a vendored vLLM 0.4.x fork pinned to PyTorch 2.0 and CUDA 12.1 with heavy custom CUDA kernels; it is impractical to install and modify for a small quality-only reproduction. The user has narrowed scope to F1 / Rouge-L on Mistral-7B fp16 against three strategies (selective recompute, full recompute, full reuse), with TTFT/throughput explicitly out of scope, which removes the only reason to depend on vLLM. Building a thin HuggingFace transformers wrapper that (a) caches per-chunk per-layer K/V in CPU tensors, (b) overrides the Mistral attention forward to apply RoPE re-rotation and selective recompute at a single check layer, and (c) drives layer-by-layer fusion via a custom forward pass, is dramatically more tractable. The official code remains a reference for exact algorithmic details (RoPE recovery, V-deviation top-r%, single check layer at index 1, in-place index assignment), which are pinned in the ambiguity log.

modules.purpose: In-memory per-(chunk_hash, layer_id) KV cache store with sha256_cbor hashing, fetch/put API, and pre-RoPE storage convention.
public_api: class ChunkKVStore:
def __init__(self, num_layers: int, dtype: torch.dtype, device: str = 'cpu')
def hash_chunk(self, token_ids: list[int], parent_hash: bytes | None = None) -> bytes
def put(self, chunk_hash: bytes, layer_id: int, k: torch.Tensor, v: torch.Tensor) -> None
def fetch(self, chunk_hash: bytes, layer_id: int) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor] | None
def has(self, chunk_hash: bytes) -> bool

modules.purpose: RoPE re-rotation helper that re-applies Mistral's rotary embedding to a stored (un-rotated) K tensor at new absolute positions; mirrors the rotary_emb(new_positions, fake_q, K_pre) call in vllm_blend/llama.py:174-179.
public_api: def recover_rope_k(k_pre: torch.Tensor, new_positions: torch.LongTensor, rotary_emb: Callable) -> torch.Tensor
def concat_chunk_kvs(per_chunk_kv: list[tuple[Tensor, Tensor]], new_positions: torch.LongTensor, rotary_emb) -> tuple[Tensor, Tensor]

modules.purpose: Core CacheBlend algorithm: layer-by-layer prefill that recomputes Q/K/V only for HKVD-selected tokens, computes V-deviation at the single check layer (idx 1), picks top-r% indices, and reuses them on later layers. Performs in-place index assignment of K/V into the loaded tensors, then runs standard full-sequence attention.
public_api: @dataclass class BlendConfig: recompute_ratio: float; check_layer: int = 1; schedule: str = 'single_check'
class CacheBlendMistral(MistralForCausalLM):
def blend_forward(self, input_ids, chunk_boundaries, per_layer_pre_kv, cfg: BlendConfig) -> tuple[Tensor, list[tuple[Tensor, Tensor]]]
def compute_v_deviation(v_new: Tensor, v_pre: Tensor) -> Tensor
def select_hkvd_indices(deviation: Tensor, r: float) -> torch.LongTensor
def selective_layer_forward(layer, hidden_states, position_ids, pre_kv_layer, hkvd_idx, status: int, rotary_emb) -> tuple[Tensor, Tensor, Tensor, torch.LongTensor]

modules.purpose: Implements the two non-CacheBlend strategies: (1) full prefill recompute via the unmodified HF Mistral forward, and (2) full KV reuse (PromptCache-style) which concatenates pre-computed per-chunk KV with RoPE recovery applied, but with NO recompute at any layer.
public_api: def full_recompute_generate(model, tokenizer, prompt: str, max_new_tokens: int) -> str
def full_reuse_generate(model, tokenizer, chunks: list[str], query: str, store: ChunkKVStore, max_new_tokens: int) -> str
def cacheblend_generate(model, tokenizer, chunks: list[str], query: str, store: ChunkKVStore, cfg: BlendConfig, max_new_tokens: int) -> str

modules.purpose: Offline (warm-up) pass that runs the Mistral model on each chunk in isolation and stores its per-layer K (pre-RoPE) and V into ChunkKVStore. This populates the cache that all three strategies will draw from.
public_api: def precompute_chunk_kv(model, tokenizer, chunk_text: str, store: ChunkKVStore) -> bytes
def precompute_all_chunks(model, tokenizer, chunks: Iterable[str], store: ChunkKVStore) -> list[bytes]

test_plan.what_it_pins_down: Same token-id list produces same sha256_cbor hash across invocations; different parent_hash yields different hash.
K and V stored at (hash, layer_id) round-trip bit-exactly; shape (num_kv_heads, chunk_len, head_dim) preserved.
Applying rotary_emb to stored pre-rotation K at new positions equals running the original Mistral attention on the same tokens placed at those positions (max abs diff < 1e-4 in fp32).
compute_v_deviation reduces (V_new - V_pre) ** 2 across heads and head_dim, giving one scalar per token (matches vllm_blend xformers.py:210).
Given a deviation vector with known ordering, select_hkvd_indices(r=0.15) returns exactly the ceil(0.15 * N) top indices.
With recompute_ratio=1.0 the layer output matches the unmodified HF Mistral layer (sanity that the layer wrapper is loss-free at the full-recompute extreme).
After key_old[imp_indices] = key_new, key_old at non-selected positions is bit-identical to its pre-assignment values (no scatter side-effects).
End-to-end CacheBlend pipeline produces a non-trivial F1 (> 0.0) on 5 2WikiMQA examples with Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 at r=0.15 without raising.
compute_f1('barack obama', 'Barack Obama', tokenizer) == 1.0; compute_f1('paris', 'london', tokenizer) == 0.0; matches the example/utils.py implementation up to tokenizer choice.
compute_rouge_l agrees with rouge_score.RougeScorer(['rougeL'], use_stemmer=True).score(...).rougeL.fmeasure on canned examples.

open_decisions.question: Which recompute-ratio grid r should we evaluate? Paper sweeps 5-18% on Yi-34B (Figure 16); the released code defaults to 0.15-0.18.
options: Single point r=0.15 (paper's stated quality floor r*)
Two-point [0.15, 0.18] matching the released example scripts

open_decisions.question: How many examples per dataset should we use? Paper uses full eval sets (2WikiMQA 200, Musique 150, SAMSum 200, MultiNews 60); a quality-only reproduction can use a subset.
options: 50 per dataset (fast iteration, ~2 hours total on 1xA40)
200 per dataset (full eval set where available; matches paper)

open_decisions.question: Which HKVD selection schedule should we implement? The ambiguity log resolved the released code uses a SINGLE check layer at decoder index 1, but the paper describes a gradual-decay schedule.
options: Single check layer at idx 1 only (matches official code; high-confidence resolution)
Check every layer with the same r% (simpler; deviates from official code but closer to paper's verbal description)
Implement both behind a flag and ablate
open_decisions.recommended: Single check layer at idx 1 only (matches official code; high-confidence resolution)

open_decisions.question: Which Mistral-7B-Instruct version should we target? Paper says 'Mistral-7B' without pinning a release; references.json lists v0.2.
options: mistralai/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.1 (closest in time to paper experiments)

open_decisions.question: How many context chunks should we concatenate per query? Paper says top-6 for the Extended datasets; the original (non-Extended) eval inputs in inputs/wikimqa_s.json carry the dataset's native context count.
options: Whatever count is in the bundled wikimqa_s.json / musique_s.json (faithful to paper's released inputs)
open_decisions.recommended: Whatever count is in the bundled wikimqa_s.json / musique_s.json (faithful to paper's released inputs); for SAMSum/MultiNews use the dataset's native chunking.

build_order: 1. Scaffold code/ tree, configs/default.yaml, pyproject or requirements.txt, and pytest harness.
2. Implement code/eval/datasets.py with the exact build_qa_prompt and build_fewshot_prompt from example/utils.py; verify on bundled wikimqa_s.json sample.
3. Implement code/eval/metrics.py (SQuAD-style F1 + Rouge-L) and tests/test_metrics.py; gate on the F1/Rouge-L unit tests.
4. Implement code/cacheblend/kv_cache.py (sha256_cbor hashing + in-memory CPU store) and tests/test_kv_cache.py.

5. Implement code/cacheblend/precompute.py: load Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 fp16, run per-chunk forward to capture pre-RoPE K and V per layer; verify shapes against expected (num_kv_heads=8, head_dim=128, num_layers=32).
6. Implement code/cacheblend/blend.py (RoPE recovery) and tests/test_rope_recovery.py; pin matches against a direct HF forward at the new positions.
7. Implement code/cacheblend/selective_recompute.py V-deviation and top-r% selection; gate on tests/test_hkvd_selector.py.
8. Implement the layer-wrapper selective_layer_forward and blend_forward; gate on tests/test_selective_recompute.py (recompute_ratio=1.0 must reproduce HF output bit-close).
9. Implement code/cacheblend/baselines.py: full_recompute_generate (unmodified HF) and full_reuse_generate (RoPE recovery only, no recompute).
10. Wire code/scripts/run_smoke.py to run 5 examples on 2WikiMQA across all three strategies and print three F1 numbers; this is the integration gate.
11. Implement code/eval/run_eval.py: iterate (dataset x strategy x r) grid from configs/default.yaml, write JSON results to workspace/results/.
12. Resolve open_decisions with user; freeze configs/default.yaml; run the full quality grid; collect and compare against reproduction_targets.
